finding.claim: update_doc overwrites a document body without enforcing edit authorization; can_edit result on line 19 is discarded, so any caller reaching the route can modify any document (CWE-862 / BOLA).
finding.source: Path parameter doc_id and JSON body field; caller needs only to reach PUT /doc/<doc_id> with g.user set.

trace.note: can_edit(g.user, doc) evaluated but boolean result discarded; no abort

finding.guards_checked: can_edit (docs.py:7-8) computed but not enforced; require_edit (docs.py:11-13) not called on this path; no decorator or before_request auth/ownership check visible in this file. Sibling update_title (docs.py:24-29) does call require_edit, so the omission is inconsistent.

verdict.guard_found: none effective. can_edit (docs.py:7-8) returns a bool, but the bare call at docs.py:19 discards it with no abort. require_edit (docs.py:11-13) is not called on the PUT /doc/<doc_id> path (only on update_title at docs.py:27). No before_request, login_required, or other auth decorator exists in the directory (Grep found none).
verdict.reason: update_doc at docs.py:19 evaluates can_edit(g.user, doc) as a bare statement and never tests the result, so docs.py:20 overwrites doc["body"] for any user who can reach PUT /doc/<doc_id>, while the sibling update_title at docs.py:27 correctly calls require_edit. The attacker is any authenticated low-privilege user, since nothing in this repo sets g.user and the route is reachable by anyone who is logged in.

The only other check, require_edit (docs.py:11-13, used at docs.py:27), is on a different route (/title). No upstream auth or ownership check is visible in the available files.
verdict.reason: The write in update_doc (docs.py:19-20) is unconditional because can_edit's result is discarded at docs.py:19, so any caller who reaches the route can overwrite any document body. The claimed mechanism is wrong, though: the None==None path at docs.py:8 is irrelevant, since the result is never tested. Anonymous reachability depends on upstream middleware not in this directory, but any authenticated low-privilege user can already exploit this as an IDOR, which is a real vulnerability.
